compatibility: Existing IContextPluginNextGen interface, default layout, hooks, signatures, saved schema, storage/event/result shapes and tool pipeline retained.
Contributions are explicitly registered beside plugins; existing similarly named methods remain untouched.
Built-in protected task/evidence/instruction views cannot be replaced; new blocks are user data and never authorization.
Host tokenizer, source caps and layout are optional. Default estimation and ordinary/direct/external ownership remain unchanged.
Sources persist using existing plugin storage. Callbacks, selected views and process-local authority/observations are not restored from sessions.
Existing model output/cache usage fields remain intact; new manifest fields are optional.
supportBoundaries: Contributors/revision getters and trusted instruction overrides are host code. Host scope and revision must track content, permission and task changes; no arbitrary private effects can be rolled back.
No sandbox/preemption of synchronous host JavaScript. Cumulative contributor timeout excludes legacy content/template hooks and compaction.
Protected component/source overflow and stale model/input/authority/dependencies fail explicitly; ordinary global fit still uses the existing bounded compactor.
Pre-preparation inspection runs no new contributors; its estimate cannot describe unknown future contributed data.
Provider cache fields use normalized observed usage, preserving absent as null and actual zero. Fingerprints are diagnostics, not provider cache keys.
Model/opaque/multimodal accounting remains estimated, with explicit provider/host/registry/fallback provenance. No automatic tuning/cache-hit/cost benefit promise.
The legacy advanced shared-context/raw-load ownership boundaries remain host responsibilities.
